title: Two routes for oxygen
hook: Animals in water do not all use the same organ.

doesNotKnow: A fish uses gills in water. Which organ does a whale use to take oxygen from air?

misconception: The first explanation of an aquatic animal feature must be correct.
objective: A fish uses gills in water. Which organ does a whale use to take oxygen from air?

claims.text: A fish uses gills in water. Which organ does a whale use to take oxygen from air? The fish panel shows water crossing gills; the whale panel shows air entering lungs. Whales are mammals that breathe air with lungs, while fish gills typically exchange gases with water. These are simplified routes, not a complete anatomy of every fish.
claims.source: Source leads, not checked: NOAA Fisheries, https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/; OpenStax Biology 2e, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The two panels are simplified schematics, not observations or measurements.
A whale surfaces and takes in air. Which organ performs gas exchange with that air? Whales are air-breathing mammals with lungs.
